properties.content: Question: cre symptoms Answer: Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE) infections can cause a wide range of symptoms depending on the location and severity of the infection. Some common symptoms include:: - Fever and chills - Fatigue - Shortness of breath - Cough - Painful urination - Abdominal pain - Nausea and vomiting - Redness, swelling, or pain at the site of infection - Meningitis (inflammation of the membranes covering the brain and spinal cord) - Sepsis (a life-threatening bloodstream infection) The specific symptoms may vary depending on the type of bacteria involved and the body system affected. For example, a CRE infection in the urinary tract may cause pain and burning during urination, while a CRE infection in the lungs may cause severe cough and shortness of breath.

Question: cre symptoms

Answer: Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE) infections can cause a wide range of symptoms depending on the location and severity of the infection. Some common symptoms include::
- Fever and chills
- Fatigue
- Shortness of breath
- Cough
- Painful urination
- Abdominal pain
- Nausea and vomiting
- Redness, swelling, or pain at the site of infection
- Meningitis (inflammation of the membranes covering the brain and spinal cord)
- Sepsis (a life-threatening bloodstream infection)
The specific symptoms may vary depending on the type of bacteria involved and the body system affected. For example, a CRE infection in the urinary tract may cause pain and burning during urination, while a CRE infection in the lungs may cause severe cough and shortness of breath.
